info.title: Ambivo Agents Core SDK
info.description:
## Overview

Core infrastructure for the Ambivo Agents SDK. Covers BaseAgent lifecycle, SSE streaming protocol,
Redis memory management, multi-provider LLM service, configuration system, and workflow orchestration.

This specification documents the HTTP API surface that wraps the `ambivo_agents` Python SDK, enabling
language-agnostic access to agent creation, chat, streaming, memory, LLM generation, file operations,
configuration, and workflow execution.

---

## BaseAgent Lifecycle

Every agent inherits from `BaseAgent` and follows a consistent lifecycle:

```python
# Factory pattern -- returns agent + context for explicit handling
agent, context = MyAgent.create(user_id="user123")
response = await agent.chat("Hello")
await agent.cleanup_session()

# Simple pattern -- context is auto-managed internally
agent = MyAgent.create_simple(user_id="user123")

# Context manager -- automatic cleanup on exit
async with AgentSession(MyAgent, user_id="user123") as agent:
    response = await agent.chat("Hello")
```

Three factory methods are available:

| Method | Returns | Use case |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `create()` | `(agent, AgentContext)` | Full control over session context |
| `create_simple()` | `agent` | Quick prototyping, context auto-managed |
| `create_advanced()` | `agent` | Inject explicit memory manager and LLM service |

---

## SSE Streaming Protocol

The streaming chat endpoint (`POST /core/agent/{agent_id}/chat/stream`) returns an `text/event-stream`
response. Clients MUST follow the wire format below.

### Named Events

These use the SSE `event:` field:

| Event name | Data | Client action |
|------------|------|---------------|
| `session` | `<session_id>` (plain string) | Store session ID internally. Do **NOT** display to user. |
| `done` | *(empty)* | Stream is finished. Close the connection. |

### Default (JSON) Events

All other frames arrive without a named `event:` field. The `data:` line contains a JSON object
with a `type` discriminator:

| `type` | Additional fields | Client action |
|--------|-------------------|---------------|
| `stream_start` | `session_id` | Show typing indicator. |
| `stream_status` | `session_id`, `status` | Show as status text (e.g. "Searching..."). Do **NOT** append to chat. |
| `keepalive` | `session_id` | Ignore. Connection keep-alive ping. |
| `stream_chunk` | `session_id`, `text` | Append `text` verbatim to the response buffer. |
| `stream_complete` | `session_id`, `answer`, `metadata` | Final answer. Replace buffer with `answer`. |
| `stream_error` | `session_id`, `error` | Display error to user. |
| `stream_cancelled` | `session_id` | Stream was cancelled server-side. |

### Critical Buffering Rule

```
buffer += data.text
```

**Never** trim, strip, or add spaces between chunks. Concatenate `text` fields exactly as received.

### Wire Format Example

```
event: session
data: ses_abc123

data: {"type":"stream_start","session_id":"ses_abc123"}

data: {"type":"stream_status","session_id":"ses_abc123","status":"Thinking..."}

data: {"type":"stream_chunk","session_id":"ses_abc123","text":"Hello"}

data: {"type":"stream_chunk","session_id":"ses_abc123","text":", world!"}

data: {"type":"stream_complete","session_id":"ses_abc123","answer":"Hello, world!","metadata":{"provider":"openai","tokens":12}}

event: done
data:
```

---

## Configuration

Two methods for configuring the SDK:

1. **YAML file** -- `agent_config.yaml` loaded automatically when `auto_configure=True`
2. **Environment variables** -- prefixed with `AMBIVO_AGENTS_` (e.g. `AMBIVO_AGENTS_REDIS_HOST`)

Environment variables override YAML values when both are present.

---

## Multi-Provider LLM

The LLM service supports multiple providers with automatic failover:

- **OpenAI** -- GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5
- **Anthropic** -- Claude 3.5, Claude 3 Opus/Sonnet/Haiku
- **AWS Bedrock** -- Claude, Titan, and other Bedrock models

Provider rotation happens automatically when a provider hits rate limits or errors.
After 3 consecutive errors a provider enters cooldown for a configurable number of minutes.

post.description:
Creates an agent instance using the standard factory pattern. Returns the agent ID,
session ID, and full agent context. This is the recommended creation method for
production use because it gives the caller explicit access to the `AgentContext`.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
agent, context = MyAgent.create(user_id="user123")
```

user_id.description: Unique identifier for the user who owns this agent session.

tenant_id.description: Tenant identifier for multi-tenant deployments. Defaults to `default` if omitted.

session_id.description:
Optional session ID to reuse an existing session. When omitted the server generates a new UUID.
Providing this allows multiple agents to share conversation context.

system_message.description: Custom system message that overrides the agent's default persona prompt.
system_message.example: You are a helpful coding assistant specializing in Python.

auto_configure.description: When `true`, the agent loads configuration from `agent_config.yaml` automatically.

agent_id.description: Unique identifier assigned to the new agent instance.

session_id.description: Session ID for this agent (generated or reused).

400.description: Invalid request (unknown agent class, missing user_id).

post.description:
Simplified agent creation that auto-manages context internally. Returns only
the agent ID. Best suited for quick prototyping or single-agent scenarios.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
agent = MyAgent.create_simple(user_id="user123")
```

agent_id.description: Unique identifier for the created agent.

post.description:
Advanced agent creation that accepts pre-configured memory manager and LLM service
instances. Use this when you need full control over shared infrastructure (e.g.
multiple agents sharing the same Redis connection pool).

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
memory = create_redis_memory_manager("agent_id")
llm = create_multi_provider_llm_service()
agent = MyAgent.create_advanced("agent_id", memory, llm)
```

memory_manager_config.description: Configuration for the Redis memory manager.

llm_service_config.description: Configuration for the multi-provider LLM service.

agent_id.description: The agent ID that was provided in the request.

delete.description:
Cleans up all resources associated with the agent session including memory,
conversation history, thread pool executors, and any cached state. This should
always be called when an agent is no longer needed.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
await agent.cleanup_session()
```

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: The agent instance ID to clean up.

cleared_memory.description: Whether conversation memory was cleared from Redis.

cleared_executor.description: Whether the thread pool executor was shut down.

post.description:
Sends a user message to the agent and returns the full response. This is the
primary high-level interface -- the agent handles routing, memory storage,
and context management internally.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
response = await agent.chat("Hello")
```

metadata.description: Optional metadata to attach to this message (e.g. source, client version).

content.example: Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that enables systems to learn and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed.

example.content: Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that enables systems to learn and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed.

example.error: LLM provider unavailable after failover attempts

post.description:
Blocking synchronous version of the chat endpoint. The server will not return
until the full response is ready. Useful for simple integrations that cannot
handle async patterns.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
response = agent.chat_sync("Hello")
```

message.example: Explain quantum computing in one sentence.

example.message: Explain quantum computing in one sentence.

content.example: Quantum computing uses quantum bits (qubits) that can exist in superposition states to perform certain computations exponentially faster than classical computers.

example.content: Quantum computing uses quantum bits (qubits) that can exist in superposition states to perform certain computations exponentially faster than classical computers.

post.description:
Sends a message and receives the response as a Server-Sent Events stream.
The client must follow the SSE protocol documented in the info section.

**Event sequence:**
1. Named event `session` with the session ID
2. JSON event `stream_start`
3. Zero or more `stream_status` events (e.g. "Thinking...", "Searching...")
4. One or more `stream_chunk` events with incremental text
5. JSON event `stream_complete` with the full answer
6. Named event `done`

**Buffering rule:** `buffer += data.text` -- never trim, strip, or insert spaces.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
async for chunk in agent.process_message_stream(message):
    print(chunk.content, end="")
```

message.example: Tell me about the history of AI.

example.message: Tell me about the history of AI.

post.description:
Sends a fully-formed `AgentMessage` object to the agent for processing and
returns the response as an `AgentMessage`. This is the low-level interface
that `chat()` is built on. Use it when you need full control over message
metadata, sender/recipient IDs, and message types.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
response_message = await agent.process_message(agent_message)
```

example.content: What is the weather like today?
I don't have access to real-time weather data. You could try asking the web search agent.

get.description:
Returns machine-readable documentation of the SSE streaming protocol including
all event types, wire format examples, and buffering rules. Useful for client
SDK generators and integration testing.

event_types.description: All SSE event types that can be emitted.

fields.description: Fields present in this event type.

action.description: Recommended client action for this event.

wire_format_examples.description: Example SSE frames as raw strings.

event_types.action: Show as status text, NOT in chat

wire_format_examples:
event: session
data: ses_abc123
data: {"type":"stream_chunk","session_id":"ses_abc123","text":"Hello"}
event: done
data:

buffering_rules.description: Never trim, strip, or add spaces between chunks. Concatenate text fields exactly as received.

post.description:
Stores a message in the Redis-backed conversation history. Messages are
compressed with LZ4 for efficient storage. Each message is keyed by
session ID and conversation ID.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
agent.memory_manager.store_message(message)
```

session_id.description: Session ID that owns this conversation.

conversation_id.description: Optional conversation thread ID within the session.

message.content: Remember that my favorite color is blue.

get.description:
Retrieves recent messages from conversation history, ordered newest first.
Results are decompressed from LZ4 on the fly.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
messages = agent.memory_manager.get_recent_messages(limit=10, conversation_id="conv_001")
```

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Session ID to retrieve messages from.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Filter to a specific conversation thread. Omit to get messages across all conversations.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 10.

messages.content: Remember that my favorite color is blue.
Got it! I'll remember that your favorite color is blue.

post.description:
Stores an arbitrary key-value pair in session context. Context values persist
across conversations within the same session and are available to all agents
sharing that session.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
agent.memory_manager.store_context("preferred_language", "Python", conversation_id="conv_001")
```

session_id.description: Session ID to store context under.

value.description: Context value. Can be a string, number, boolean, array, or object.

get.description:
Retrieves a context value by key for the given session.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
value = agent.memory_manager.get_context("preferred_language")
```

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Session ID to look up context from.

404.description: Key not found for this session.

delete.description:
Clears all messages and context for a session or specific conversation.
When `conversation_id` is provided, only that conversation's data is removed.
When omitted, all conversations in the session are cleared.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
agent.memory_manager.clear_memory(conversation_id="conv_001")
```

conversation_id.description: Optional conversation ID to scope the clear operation.

post.description:
Generates a response using the multi-provider LLM service. The service automatically
selects the best available provider based on priority, rate limits, and error state.
You can optionally force a specific provider.

Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, and AWS Bedrock providers with automatic failover.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
response = await llm_service.generate_response(prompt, context)
```

prompt.description: The prompt text to send to the LLM.
prompt.example: Explain the difference between REST and GraphQL APIs.

system_message.description: Optional system message to set the LLM's persona.
system_message.example: You are a senior software architect.

conversation_history.description: Optional prior conversation messages for context.

example.content: An API (Application Programming Interface) is a set of protocols and tools for building software applications.

provider.description: Force a specific LLM provider. Omit for automatic selection.

example.prompt: Explain the difference between REST and GraphQL APIs.
example.system_message: You are a senior software architect.

content.example: REST uses fixed endpoints with HTTP methods, while GraphQL uses a single endpoint with a query language that lets clients request exactly the data they need.

provider_used.description: The provider that actually served this request.

example.content: REST uses fixed endpoints with HTTP methods, while GraphQL uses a single endpoint with a query language that lets clients request exactly the data they need.

example.error: All LLM providers are currently unavailable. Providers in cooldown.

post.description:
Generates a streaming response using the multi-provider LLM service. Returns
an SSE stream of text chunks as they are generated by the LLM.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
async for chunk in llm_service.generate_response_stream(prompt, context):
    print(chunk, end="")
```

prompt.description: The prompt text to send to the LLM.
prompt.example: Write a haiku about distributed systems.

example.prompt: Write a haiku about distributed systems.

get.description:
Returns the current status of all configured LLM providers, including
availability, request counts, error counts, and cooldown state.

post.description:
Reads a file from a local path or remote URL. Supports TXT, JSON, CSV, XML,
and YAML formats. Remote files are fetched via HTTP/HTTPS. Automatic encoding
detection is applied for local files.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
result = await agent.read_file("path/to/file.txt")
# or
result = await agent.read_file("https://example.com/data.json")
```

file_path.description:
Local file path or remote URL. Local paths can be absolute or relative
(resolved against configured base directories). URLs must start with `http://` or `https://`.

success.description: Whether the file was read without errors.

content.description: Raw file content as a string.

400.description: Unsupported file type or unreadable content.

post.description:
Parses raw file content according to the specified format. Returns structured
data with metadata about the parsed result.

Supported formats:
- **json** -- Returns parsed JSON with structure metadata
- **csv** -- Returns list of dictionaries with column info
- **xml** -- Converts to nested dictionary structure
- **yaml** -- Full YAML parsing
- **text** -- Returns content with line and character counts

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
result = await agent.parse_file_content(content, "csv")
```

file_type.description: Format to parse the content as.

data.description: Parsed data structure. Shape depends on the file_type.

400.description: Parse error or unsupported file type.

example.error: Failed to parse content as json: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes

post.description:
Converts data between supported formats. Currently supports JSON-to-CSV and
CSV-to-JSON conversions with automatic type inference.

Equivalent SDK calls:
```python
csv_data = await agent.convert_json_to_csv(json_data)
json_data = await agent.convert_csv_to_json(csv_content)
```

data.description:
The data to convert. For JSON-to-CSV this should be an array of objects.
For CSV-to-JSON this should be a CSV string.

converted.description: The converted data. String for CSV output, array/object for JSON output.

get.description:
Returns the full merged configuration from `agent_config.yaml` and any
environment variable overrides. Sensitive values (API keys, passwords) are
masked in the response.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
from ambivo_agents.config.loader import load_config
config = load_config()
```

Returns a specific configuration section. Valid sections include `redis`, `llm`,
`knowledge_base`, `docker`, `agent_capabilities`, `web_search`, `analytics`,
and `api_agent`.

post.description:
Creates a new workflow definition with nodes (agents) and edges (connections).
Workflows support sequential, parallel, conditional, and loop execution patterns.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
workflow = WorkflowBuilder()
    .add_agent(search_agent, "search")
    .add_agent(scraper_agent, "scrape")
    .add_edge("search", "scrape")
    .build()
```

nodes.description: Workflow nodes, each representing an agent or control node.

id.description: Unique node identifier within this workflow.

agent_class.description: Agent class to instantiate for this node.

condition.description: Optional condition expression. Edge is followed only when condition evaluates to true.

weight.description: Edge weight for priority ordering (lower is higher priority).

execution_type.description: How the workflow nodes should be executed.

workflow_id.description: Unique identifier for the created workflow.

400.description: Invalid workflow definition (e.g. cyclic graph, unknown agent class).

example.error: Cyclic dependency detected between nodes: search -> scrape -> search

post.description:
Executes a previously created workflow with the given input message and context.
The workflow engine processes nodes according to the execution type (sequential,
parallel, conditional, or loop) and returns the aggregated result.

Equivalent SDK call:
```python
result = await workflow.execute(message, context)
```

message.description: Input message to the first workflow node.
message.example: Research the latest developments in quantum computing

example.message: Research the latest developments in quantum computing

messages.content: Found 5 relevant articles about quantum computing advances.
Scraped content from 4 of 5 URLs successfully.
Ingested 4 documents into the quantum_computing knowledge base.

BearerAuth.description:
JWT bearer token issued by Ambivo authentication service. Include in the
`Authorization` header as `Bearer <token>`.

AgentMessage.description:
Core message object used for all agent communication. Every message has a sender,
optional recipient, content, type, and session context. This is the fundamental
data structure that flows through the entire agent system.

id.description: Unique message identifier, typically a UUID.

sender_id.description: ID of the message sender (user ID or agent ID).

recipient_id.description: ID of the intended recipient. Null for broadcast messages.

message_type.description: Discriminator for how the message should be processed.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata attached to this message.

session_id.description: Session ID this message belongs to.

conversation_id.description: Conversation thread ID within the session.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the message was created.

StreamChunk.description:
A single chunk in the SSE streaming protocol. Each chunk has a `type` discriminator
that tells the client how to handle it. Chunks arrive as JSON in the `data:` field
of SSE frames.

type.description:
Event type discriminator. Determines what fields are present and how the
client should handle this chunk.

text.description:
Incremental text content (present only for `stream_chunk` type).
Must be appended to the buffer exactly as received -- no trimming or spacing.

answer.description: Complete final answer (present only for `stream_complete` type).
answer.example: Machine learning is a branch of AI that learns from data.

sub_type.description: Sub-classification of the chunk for fine-grained client handling.

metadata.description: Additional metadata for the chunk (e.g. token counts, provider info).

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this chunk was generated.

ExecutionContext.description:
Execution context passed to agents and workflows. Contains session identity
and arbitrary metadata for the current operation.

session_id.description: Broader user session or application context identifier.

conversation_id.description: Specific conversation thread within the session.

AgentContext.description:
Built-in context for every BaseAgent instance. Automatically created when an
agent is instantiated via a factory method. Contains all identity information
and can be converted to an `ExecutionContext` for operations.

session_id.description: Session ID assigned to this agent.

conversation_id.description: Default conversation ID for this agent.

agent_id.description: Unique identifier for this agent instance.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the agent was created.

metadata.description: Additional agent metadata that can be updated via `update_metadata()`.

ProviderConfig.description:
Configuration and runtime status for an LLM provider. Tracks request counts,
error rates, and cooldown state for automatic failover decisions.

model_name.description: The specific model used by this provider.

priority.description: Provider priority (lower number = higher priority). Used for selection order.

available.description: Whether the provider is currently available for requests.

total_requests.description: Total number of requests made to this provider since startup.

total_errors.description: Total number of errors from this provider since startup.

cooldown_until.description:
If the provider is in cooldown, this is the ISO 8601 timestamp when it becomes
available again. Null when the provider is not in cooldown.

max_requests_per_minute.description: Rate limit -- maximum requests per minute.

max_requests_per_hour.description: Rate limit -- maximum requests per hour.

cooldown_minutes.description: Number of minutes a provider stays in cooldown after repeated errors.

MemoryStats.description:
Performance and usage statistics for the Redis memory manager. Tracks cache
efficiency, operation counts, and error rates.

total_operations.description: Total number of memory operations (reads + writes) since startup.

cache_hits.description: Number of operations served from the local TTL cache.

cache_misses.description: Number of operations that required a Redis round-trip.

error_count.description: Number of memory operations that resulted in errors.

cache_hit_rate.description: Cache hit rate as a percentage (0.0 - 100.0). Computed as `cache_hits / (cache_hits + cache_misses) * 100`.

compression_savings_bytes.description: Total bytes saved by LZ4 compression of stored messages.

avg_response_time_ms.description: Average response time in milliseconds for memory operations.

redis_memory_usage_bytes.description: Current Redis memory usage in bytes for this agent's keys.

local_cache_size.description: Number of entries currently in the local TTL cache.

WorkflowResult.description:
Result of a workflow execution. Contains the success status, all messages
produced during execution, timing information, and any errors encountered.

success.description: Whether the workflow completed without critical errors.

messages.description: All agent messages produced during workflow execution, in chronological order.

execution_time.description: Total wall-clock execution time in seconds.

nodes_executed.description: Ordered list of node IDs that were executed.

errors.description: List of non-fatal error messages encountered during execution.

metadata.description: Additional execution metadata (e.g. counts, execution type).

ConfigSection.description:
Complete configuration object representing all sections of `agent_config.yaml`.
Each top-level key is a configuration section. Sensitive values (API keys,
passwords) are masked when returned via the API.

redis.description: Redis connection settings for the memory management system.

password.description: Redis authentication password (masked in API responses).

llm.description: LLM provider configuration including available providers and defaults.

providers.description: List of enabled LLM provider names.

preferred_provider.description: Default provider to try first before failover.

temperature.description: Default sampling temperature for LLM responses.

knowledge_base.description: Qdrant vector database settings for the knowledge base agent.

qdrant_url.description: URL of the Qdrant vector database instance.

chunk_size.description: Maximum number of tokens per text chunk for ingestion.

docker.description: Docker container execution settings for sandboxed agent operations.

shared_base_dir.description: Base directory for Docker shared volumes.

images.description: Docker image mappings for each agent type.

agent_capabilities.description: Feature flags to enable or disable specific agent capabilities.

media_processing.description: Enable media processing agent (requires FFmpeg in Docker).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error response returned by all endpoints on failure.

code.description: Machine-readable error code for programmatic handling.
